events.p: 191 km ENE of Nagqu, Tibet, China
events.sum: A shallow (18 km) magnitude 7.0 quake struck a remote, mountainous part of northern Tibet at night. At least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed. GDACS issued a red alert, estimating about 10,000 people were exposed to very strong (MMI VII+) shaking.
events.deaths: At least 16 dead; up to 65 injured

econ.v: No published estimate. USGS PAGER issued an orange alert, a band that corresponds to USD 100 million–1 billion in losses or 100–999 deaths

ins.v: No estimate published; insurance penetration in the area is very low

events.p: Guam & Northern Mariana Islands; approaching Taiwan, East China, Japan
events.sum: Champi passed about 12 miles off southern Guam on 17–18 Oct, damaging homes, cutting power and water and putting up to 170 wells out of service. More than 1,000 people sheltered across four islands. It then became the strongest storm on Earth this year, peaking at 185 mph, and is tracking toward Taiwan, eastern China and southern Japan.

ins.v: Not yet estimated; Moody's RMS is tracking the event

mr.nt: Forecast impacts on Taiwan, eastern China, southern Japan and South Korea

events.p: Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Nice and other cities
events.sum: Protests over living costs and public services turned into rioting, looting and arson on 17–18 Oct. More than 1,500 buildings were damaged. For insurers this is a strikes, riots and civil commotion (SRCC) loss, with five départements holding about 45% of the damaged properties.

mr.nt: An estimated 550,000 to 800,000 people participated in the protests which were organized by a coalition of Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and student groups.

events.p: Landfall near Destin, Florida Panhandle, USA
events.sum: Isaias came ashore near Destin on the evening of 9 Oct (local time) as a Category 2 hurricane. Falling trees, debris and roof-cover loss caused most damage across the Florida Panhandle; wind drives the bulk of the insured loss.

mr.nt: AM Pre-Landfall SSEs #1 10/8/2026 12:00:00 AM Custom Events | Summary Posting Date: October 13, 2026, 12:00:00 PM Verisk estimates that insured industry losses to onshore property for Hurricane Isaias will fall between USD 1 billion and USD 2 billion. · Verisk loss estimate: USD 1–2 billion

events.p: 12 km WSW of Pitaloza Arriba, southern Panama
events.sum: The strongest quake in the sequence hit southern Panama on 9 Oct, followed by M6.6, M6.0 and M6.1 aftershocks over four days. About 900 homes and hundreds of schools, clinics and bridges were damaged across nine provinces; Panama declared a state of emergency.

econ.v: No published estimate. USGS PAGER issued an orange alert (USD 100 million–1 billion band or 100–999 deaths)

ins.v: Not published; Verisk provided modeling event IDs only

events.p: Offshore west coast of Mexico (Guerrero to Jalisco)
events.sum: Simon reached major-hurricane strength but stayed offshore as it passed Mexico's Pacific coast on 11 Oct, dissipating on 16 Oct.

events.p: Baja California and Mexico's Pacific coast
events.sum: Polo affected Baja California and the Pacific coast of Mexico on 28–29 Sep.

events.p: Pacific coast of Japan incl. Tokyo
events.sum: Dujuan brushed Japan's Pacific coast on 21 Sep, bringing heavy rain and flooding to the Tokyo area.

events.p: Near Niʻihau and Kauaʻi, Hawaiʻi, USA
events.sum: Lowell passed close to Niʻihau and Kauaʻi on 8 Sep, the second hurricane threat to Hawaiʻi within a month.

events.p: Zhejiang province, China
events.sum: Saudel made landfall in Zhejiang on 28 Aug.

events.p: Hawaiʻi Island (Big Island) and Oʻahu, USA
events.sum: Lala skirted the Big Island on 15 Aug without making landfall but dropped up to 43 inches of rain. About 100 homes were damaged or washed away, six bridges and roads were destroyed or badly damaged, part of a highway collapsed and some 200,000 customers lost power.

events.p: Off Flores, 68 km NNW of Ende, Indonesia
events.sum: A shallow (~10 km) M7.7 quake struck off Flores Island on 15 Aug, damaging more than 1,300 homes and displacing thousands.

events.p: Northern Venezuela: La Guaira, Caracas, Carabobo
events.sum: Two large quakes struck a minute apart on the evening of 24 Jun, the stronger being Venezuela's biggest since 1900. Buildings collapsed in Caracas and La Guaira; over 850 buildings were damaged and 190 collapsed, and more than 23,500 people moved into camps. It is the deadliest catastrophe of 2026 so far.

econ.v: USD 6.7 billion direct physical damage (~6% of GDP)

ins.v: Not published; insurance penetration is low

events.p: Central & eastern USA incl. Illinois and Indiana
events.sum: A week-long outbreak of tornadoes, hail and damaging winds from 23 to 29 Apr, part of a severe-storm season that cost US insurers about USD 27 billion in the first half of 2026.

econ.v: Not published separately (H1 2026 US SCS total: USD 34 billion)

events.p: Portugal (Leiria landfall), Spain, Morocco and the Mediterranean
events.sum: Kristin made landfall in Portugal's Leiria district on the night of 28 Jan, becoming Portugal's costliest windstorm on record, with flooding driving much of the loss across Iberia.

econ.v: More than €7.2 billion (Portugal €6 bn+, Spain ~€1.2 bn)

events.p: Eastern & southern USA, Texas to Massachusetts
events.sum: Fern brought freezing rain, heavy snow and severe thunderstorms across much of the eastern and southern US from 23 to 26 Jan. Freezing (burst pipes, ice) drives most of the insured damage.

events.p: Off NW Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu
events.sum: A vigorous swarm of more than 25 M4.5+ quakes began on 19 Oct about 200 km off Espiritu Santo, peaking with an M6.3 on 20 Oct. GDACS rated the largest shocks green.

events.p: 76 km NE of Ozernovskiy, Kamchatka, Russia
events.sum: An intermediate-depth (135 km) quake beneath southern Kamchatka; depth limited the shaking and no damage was reported.

events.p: Central Mid-Atlantic Ridge
events.sum: Two strong quakes on the remote Mid-Atlantic Ridge on 13 Oct; far from land, no impact.

events.p: 48 km WNW of Khuzdar, Balochistan, Pakistan
events.sum: A shallow quake in Balochistan; USGS PAGER issued a yellow alert, meaning some damage and casualties were possible.
